scope: Targeted representative claims, not a complete sentence-level claim inventory. Source IDs below refer to research-module aliases and resolve through records/artifacts/source-aliases.json.

claims.subject: pi0.7 architecture, inheritance and coaching
claims.evidence: Paper sections IV and VI explicitly retain pi0.6 architecture, incorporate MEM history/memory, and use a BAGEL-based visual-subgoal generator. Section VI-A explicitly includes pi-star-0.6 RL experience for behavioral distillation. Unseen appliance tasks initially use stepwise coaching; collected coaching episodes subsequently support autonomous high-level-policy adaptation.
claims.assessment: The submitted text and explicit inheritance edges are supported. Keep coached task execution separate from unassisted zero-shot autonomy. The paper's data reuse must not be described as direct RL-specialist weight inheritance.

claims.subject: MEM / pi0.6-MEM
claims.evidence: Official research page names pi0.6 augmented with visual short-term and language long-term memory, including tasks of up to 15 minutes.
claims.assessment: The report correctly distinguishes the demonstrated task-history mechanism from general lifelong personal memory.

claims.subject: GR00T N1.7 data, backbone, availability and license
claims.date: 2026-07-07 engineering article; repository inspected at cutoff
claims.evidence: Official engineering material describes Cosmos-Reason2-2B/Qwen3-VL, a roughly 3B model, 32K hours of real/human data plus 8K simulation and deployment exports. Current repository calls N1.7 GA. Its License section separates Apache 2.0 code from NVIDIA Open Model License weights.
claims.assessment: The initial phrase GA and Apache 2.0 was insufficiently specific for weights. Editor corrected both language chapters during this audit. The N1.6 backbone naming disagreement between version-specific documentation and later broad marketing copy is correctly retained as uncertainty.

claims.subject: Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6
claims.date: 2026-04; model card and announcement dates are separately recorded
claims.evidence: The official model card identifies Gemini 3.0 Flash as its foundation and text as output.
claims.assessment: It is an embodied-reasoning model, not a motor action decoder. The text preserves this distinction.

claims.subject: Gemini Robotics 2 whole-body VLA
claims.evidence: The official announcement distinguishes a whole-body VLA from ER and on-device variants, reports tests across embodiments, and describes controlled early access. Task-level performance varies substantially.
claims.assessment: The report does not equate a release announcement with general public weights or universal task reliability.

claims.subject: Gemini Robotics ER 2 and On-Device 2 branch separation
claims.evidence: ER 2 is based on Gemini 3.5 Flash and produces text. On-Device 2 explicitly combines on-device Gemma and Gemini Robotics 1.5 technology and produces numerical actions for trusted testers.
claims.assessment: The technology-inheritance edge from Robotics 1.5 to On-Device 2 is directly supported. Do not infer that On-Device 2 is simply a quantized Robotics 2 checkpoint.

claims.subject: LingBot-VLA 2.0 architecture and scale
claims.evidence: Paper describes Qwen3-VL, sparse MoE action-expert components, a 55D canonical state/action representation and 60K retained hours, comprising 50K robot and 10K egocentric data. Its evaluation includes nine GM100 tasks.
claims.assessment: The retained training quantity is not confused with raw collected data; internal task scope is preserved instead of extrapolating to all manipulation.

claims.subject: SONIC / GEAR-SONIC 2026 engineering updates
claims.evidence: Current official repository lists the N1.7 collection/fine-tuning/execution workflow, SONIC v1.1 heading-normalization and wrist augmentation, and later per-motor gain scaling.
claims.assessment: The repository source date represents an inspected update, not the original SONIC research release. The chapter correctly separates the original N1.5 proof of concept from later N1.7 engineering integration.

claims.subject: Helix 02 hierarchy, clock rates and evidence level
claims.evidence: Official page specifies semantic S2, full-body joint targets at 200 Hz from S1, and a 1 kHz S0 controller trained with over 1,000 hours of retargeted human motion and simulated RL.
claims.assessment: The four-minute autonomous demonstration is correctly described as a vendor demonstration rather than a multi-environment reliability benchmark. The report does not collapse the three rates into a single VLA inference rate.

claims.subject: Skild S1 context training and date
claims.date: 2026-08-18 confirmed by official blog index; article citation gives August 2026
claims.evidence: Official article describes episodic demonstration-conditioned pretraining, video prompts and unchanged weights at inference. It does not publish a complete action architecture. Its quantitative scaling study reports cumulative per-step success with human failure recovery during rollouts.
claims.assessment: The current chapter avoids reproducing headline success rates and therefore makes no invalid benchmark comparison. Add the evaluation-protocol caveat if the expanded report or catalog quotes 66%, 96%, 7x, or the 380-demonstration equivalence.

claims.subject: Generalist GEN-1.5 memory, prompting and adaptation
claims.evidence: Official page describes 30-second memory, 100 Hz action trajectories and physical prompts containing sensor data plus action trajectories. It claims no explicit ICL objective and acknowledges short tasks and brittleness relative to fine-tuning.
claims.assessment: The report correctly contrasts the training recipe with S1 and does not equate sensorimotor prompting with arbitrary video imitation. GEN-1 task-adapted reliability and GEN-1.5 one-shot results are treated as different conditions.

claims.subject: BMW Figure 03 deployment vs Figure 02 historical production metrics
claims.evidence: BMW describes the new Figure 03 logistics sequencing project separately from prior Figure 02 body-shop deployment and its contribution to over 30,000 vehicles.
claims.assessment: The chapter's distinction is justified. Do not transfer the older F02 throughput or production counts to F03 or to a new Helix model version.

claims.subject: V-JEPA 2.1 planning
claims.evidence: Reuse of predictor architecture and protocol with retraining; 70% uses about 3s planning and 80% about 14s.
claims.assessment: Ten tasks per skill; no inherited predictor weights or universal real-time control claim.

claims.subject: MolmoAct2 training stages
claims.evidence: Molmo2-ER backbone, discrete autoregressive pretraining and continuous flow expert are distinct stages; Think is a separate variant.
claims.assessment: Intermediate checkpoints do not independently establish causal contribution of each stage.

claims.subject: 1XWM January2026 disclosure
claims.evidence: Video generation followed by inverse dynamics grounds generated futures into NEO actions.
claims.assessment: Disclosed runtime is slower than the generated horizon; longer closed-loop replanning remains future work.

claims.subject: RoboCasa365 version
claims.assessment: Benchmark results must report the version/horizon rather than be directly merged.
